newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Three killed, thousands flee Zaire fighting.
newsitem.headline: Three killed, thousands flee Zaire fighting.

text.p: Up to 26,400 mainly Burundi refugees fled their camp near the eastern Zairean town of Uvira on Friday after fighting between the Zairean military and ethnic Tutsi rebels left three dead, senior aid workers said.
"I can confirm that Kagunga camp is now empty because of the fighting," said Fernando Del Mundo, spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR in Geneva.
Three people were confirmed dead in the fighting and a number of Banyamulenge were taken prisoner, the aid worker said. The Banyamulenge are ethnic Tutsis.
A Hercules C-130 plane carrying medical field equipment for the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was shot at on takeoff in Uvira but it managed to leave, aid workers said.
The fighting was the second major round in Zaire in a week. Last Sunday about 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire after it was attacked by armed men.
Four refugees were killed and six wounded in the attack on Runingo camp," according to a U.N. source.
Del Mundo said Runingo was also still empty.

"The Banyamulenge came down from the mountains to find food and to rob and they were supported by people from the Burundian side and the Zairean military attacked and sent them back to the hills," a senior aid worker told Reuters from Uvira.
An aid worker based in the Burundian capital with contacts in Uvira described the situation as "extremely tense."

Fighting between Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean authorities trying to drive an estimated 200,000 Banyamulenge from a plateau west of Lake Tanganyika has left Zaire's South Kivu region in a virtual state of war.
The refugee population at Kagunga comprised of 24,000 Burundians and 2,400 Rwandans, according to UNHCR figures.
Most of these were on the move but a humanitarian source said that while all women and children left, some men remained.
There is a total of 13 camps with a total population of 219,000 in the Uvira area, the UNHCR says.
Relief sources said military men attempted to infiltrate into Zaire from Burundi on Thursday night and a number of trucks were seen on the Burundian side of the border with Zaire.
"There was a firefight between these people and Zairean soldiers. This morning, there were reports of small arms and automatic weapons in the vicinity," one source said.
Dozens have died and aid workers and diplomats fear the fighting could precipitate a wider regional conflict involving Rwanda. Heavy firing was also reported at other camps, another aid worker said.
Witnesses told Reuters this month that about 1,000 armed fighters, believed to be Banyamulenge, crossed into Zaire from Burundi on the night of September 20-21 near Uvira.
Both Rwandan and Burundian refugees languish in camps north of Uvira, a town in the delta to the north west of Lake Tanganyika surrounded by steep hills.

Runingo is one of the camps in South Kivu province which are home to about 230,000 Hutu refugees, mostly from Burundi but some from Rwanda. It is close to the border with Burundi whose Tutsi-led military regime says the camps are bases for Hutu rebels striking into Burundi.

Zaire accuses the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda, Burundi's northern neighbour, of training and arming the Banyamulenge guerrillas. Zaire's ragged army is fighting Banyamulenge guerrillas who are resisting the order to leave Zaire and return to Rwanda, a land they left as long as 200 years ago.
